description:
FILED s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), found probing #562.  PRE-EXISTING,
SILENT, and general -- it has nothing to do with caret names, they are just
where it showed up.

REPRO:
    our $x = 5; our @x = (9);
    *x = *neverdefinedglob;
    print "after=[$x] arr=[@x] def=", (defined $x ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl: after=[] arr=[] def=0
  PCL:  after=[5] arr=[9] def=1

perl's `*A = *B` REPLACES A's glob with B's -- A becomes another name for the
same GV -- so a slot B does not have is a slot A no longer has.  PCL's
p-glob-copy copies slot by slot and each copy is guarded by `boundp`, so an
UNSET source slot leaves the destination's old value in place.

WHERE IT BITES A REAL TEST: t/re/pat.t:1715 is
`*^R = *caretRglobwithnoscalar;` -- the source glob has no scalar slot ON
PURPOSE (the name says so), and perl's point is that $^R becomes undef.  Under
PCL, $^R keeps whatever it held.  Three of the four lines of the s448o probe
match perl exactly; this is the fourth.

It is also the SAME shortcoming docs/not-supported.md names in the English.pm
section ("Closing this needs true glob-to-glob aliasing (*A = *B sharing one
entry rather than copying slots)") -- so this task and @ARG's gap are one
piece of work, not two.

TWO SHAPES, and the cheap one may be enough:
  (a) CLEAR-THEN-COPY: p-glob-copy makes every slot the source does not have
      empty (scalar -> a fresh undef box, array -> empty vector, hash -> empty
      table, code -> fmakunbound).  Closes the repro.  It does NOT make the two
      names one entry, so a LATER write through B is still invisible through A.
  (b) ONE ENTRY: the glob becomes a first-class object both names point at.
      That is the boxed-aggregate/glob-value family's work, not a filler.
Probe (a) against the whole *A = *B population before shipping: p-glob-copy is
on the import path (`*{"${caller}::$name"} = \&sub`) and a clear-then-copy that
fires on the wrong shape would empty a real slot.  Also probe what perl does
for `*A = *B` where B has SOME slots and A has others.

BAR: the repro above plus an import-shaped case (`*dst = \&src` and
`*dst = *src` where src has only CODE), vs perl; a row in
Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t; cl/ change, so the full sweep + the op/ companion
leg.


RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): shape (a) CLEAR-THEN-COPY approved -- docs/computed-magic-design-s449.md SS5.  Glob-to-glob arm ONLY (the import path goes through the functionp arm, untouched -- probe it anyway); clear only slots BOUND on the destination (never create variables perl does not); empties = p-glob-undef-name-s (fresh undef box / empty vector / empty table / fmakunbound + declared-subs removal / *p-filehandles* removal).  Shape (b) one-GV stays with the boxed-aggregate/glob-value family, post-v0.1.  Implement in the SAME round-8 session as #561 (pat.t:1715 needs both).

DONE s450t (Opus, round 8 agent T), commit "s450t (Opus): #602 â `*A = *B`
REPLACES A's glob, so p-glob-copy CLEARS the slots B lacks".  Shape (a) as
ruled (docs/computed-magic-design-s449.md SS5).

p-glob-copy is CLEAR-THEN-COPY, split into %p-glob-copy-code-slot /
%p-glob-copy-var-slot / %p-glob-copy-io-slot plus one shared
%p-glob-empty-slot that `undef *foo` (p-glob-undef-name) now reads too -- ONE
reading of "what an empty slot holds" (rule 11), with an unknown sigil an
error rather than a nil (rule 12).

TWO RULES THE PROBES SETTLED, both now in the code's comments:
  * The clear fires on the GLOB-TO-GLOB arm ONLY.  `*dst = \&sub`,
    `*dst = \$scalar`, `*dst = \@a` go through %p-glob-assign-slots' typed
    arms, touch ONE slot, and are untouched -- that is the import path, and a
    clear firing there would empty a live variable.  Probed vs perl: identical
    before and after.
  * The clear only empties a destination slot ALREADY BOUND.  `*A = *B` never
    CREATES a variable perl would not (probed: `defined $c3` is false after
    `*c3 = *neverdefinedglob2`, and no $c3 comes into being).

Seven-shape probe vs perl 5.40.3 identical, INCLUDING t/re/pat.t:1715's own
`*^R = *caretRglobwithnoscalar` (the motivating row), except
`exists $main::{c3}` -- a pre-existing stash-modelling difference, verified
unchanged by this commit.

GUARD: Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t 21 -> 26 rows, incl. the negative row for the
reference/import forms.

STILL OPEN: shape (b), the two names sharing ONE ENTRY so a later write
through B is visible through A.  That stays with the boxed-aggregate /
glob-value family (post-v0.1) and is what English.pm's @ARG gap waits on --
docs/not-supported.md was updated to say so precisely.
subject: *A = *B does not CLEAR the slots B lacks: perl replaces the whole glob, PCL copies bound slots only (*x = *undefined leaves $x untouched)
